questions.prompt: Which SI unit is used to measure force?
options: Newton
Joule
Watt
Pascal
questions.correctAnswer: Newton
questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons. A newton is the force needed to give a mass of one kilogram an acceleration of one metre per second squared.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify SI units used for common physical quantities.

questions.prompt: In an investigation on how light intensity affects photosynthesis, which factor is the independent variable?
options: Light intensity
Rate of photosynthesis
Type of plant
Volume of water used
questions.correctAnswer: Light intensity
questions.explanation: The independent variable is the factor deliberately changed by the investigator. The response measured is the rate of photosynthesis.
questions.learningOutcome: Distinguish independent, dependent, and controlled variables in experiments.

questions.prompt: Why should a learner repeat measurements and calculate a mean value during a science practical?
options: To reduce the effect of random errors
To change the independent variable many times
To avoid recording units
To make the apparatus heavier
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce the effect of random errors
questions.explanation: Repeating measurements helps reveal unusual readings and makes the mean more reliable than a single measurement.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how repeated measurements improve reliability of scientific data.

questions.prompt: A cup and liquid together have a mass of 176 g. The empty cup has a mass of 42 g. What is the mass of the liquid?
questions.explanation: The mass of the liquid is found by subtracting the cup mass from the combined mass: 176 g minus 42 g equals 134 g.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate the mass of a substance from direct measurement data.

questions.prompt: A pendulum takes 18.0 s to complete 10 oscillations. What is the period of one oscillation?
questions.explanation: The period is total time divided by the number of oscillations. Dividing 18.0 s by 10 gives 1.8 s.
questions.learningOutcome: Determine the period of an oscillating system from measured data.

questions.prompt: A learner observes that water boils at a lower temperature on a high mountain than at sea level. Which conclusion is best supported?
options: Lower atmospheric pressure lowers the boiling point of water
Mountain water contains no dissolved gases
Thermometers stop working at high altitude
Water molecules become heavier on mountains
questions.correctAnswer: Lower atmospheric pressure lowers the boiling point of water
questions.explanation: Boiling occurs when vapour pressure equals external pressure. Lower atmospheric pressure allows boiling at a lower temperature.
questions.learningOutcome: Draw evidence-based conclusions from observations of physical change.

questions.prompt: Which flaw would make a fertiliser investigation on maize seedlings unreliable?
options: Giving the fertilised plants more water than the control plants
Using maize seeds from the same packet
Measuring seedling height every two days
Keeping both groups under the same light
questions.correctAnswer: Giving the fertilised plants more water than the control plants
questions.explanation: A fair test should change only the fertiliser condition. Changing water as well makes it unclear which factor affected growth.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate investigation designs for control of variables.

questions.prompt: A data set for seedling height is 12.1 cm, 12.0 cm, 12.2 cm, 18.7 cm, and 12.1 cm. What should the learner do first about 18.7 cm?
options: Check whether it was a recording or measurement error
Delete it without comment
Double every value in the table
Use it as the only result
questions.correctAnswer: Check whether it was a recording or measurement error
questions.explanation: The value is far from the pattern, so it may be anomalous. It should be checked before deciding how to treat it.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse data sets to identify and respond to anomalous readings.

questions.prompt: Which plan best compares two brands of solar lamps in a school science project?
options: Charge both for the same time under the same light and measure how long each powers an identical bulb
Charge one in sunlight and one in a cupboard, then ask learners which looks brighter
Use different bulbs and stop timing when the first learner leaves
Measure only the colour of the lamp casing
questions.correctAnswer: Charge both for the same time under the same light and measure how long each powers an identical bulb
questions.explanation: The plan controls charging conditions and load while measuring a useful output. That makes the comparison fair and evidence-based.
questions.learningOutcome: Design controlled investigations for comparing performance of simple technologies.

questions.prompt: Why are SI units important when Kenyan learners share science results with other schools or countries?
options: They provide a common standard for comparing measurements
They make all experiments have the same result
They remove the need for instruments
They change qualitative observations into opinions
questions.correctAnswer: They provide a common standard for comparing measurements
questions.explanation: Standard units allow measurements from different places to be understood and compared without confusion.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of standard units in scientific communication.

questions.prompt: Which organelle releases usable energy during aerobic respiration in eukaryotic cells?
options: Mitochondrion
Nucleus
Ribosome
Golgi body
questions.correctAnswer: Mitochondrion
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the main sites of aerobic respiration, where energy from food is transferred to ATP.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify cell organelles and state their functions.

questions.prompt: What does it mean when the cell membrane is described as selectively permeable?
options: It allows some substances to pass more easily than others
It prevents all substances from entering the cell
It changes into a cell wall during osmosis
It stores all genetic information
questions.correctAnswer: It allows some substances to pass more easily than others
questions.explanation: A selectively permeable membrane controls movement across the cell boundary, helping maintain internal conditions.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the role of selective permeability in cells.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes osmosis?
options: Movement of water through a partially permeable membrane from dilute solution to concentrated solution
Movement of oxygen through air from cold regions to hot regions
Movement of mineral ions using energy from respiration
Movement of large food particles into a cell by engulfing
questions.correctAnswer: Movement of water through a partially permeable membrane from dilute solution to concentrated solution
questions.explanation: Osmosis is a special type of diffusion involving water molecules moving across a partially permeable membrane.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe osmosis using concentration gradients and membranes.

questions.prompt: Red blood cells placed in a concentrated salt solution shrink. What explains this observation?
options: Water leaves the cells by osmosis
Salt enters the nucleus and divides it
The cell wall pulls inward
Haemoglobin changes into starch
questions.correctAnswer: Water leaves the cells by osmosis
questions.explanation: The concentrated salt solution has lower water potential than the cell contents, so water moves out through the membrane.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply osmosis to explain changes in animal cells placed in different solutions.

questions.prompt: Why do root hair cells sometimes use active transport to absorb mineral ions from soil water?
options: The ions may need to move against their concentration gradient using energy
The ions are too large to exist in soil
Active transport only happens in dead cells
Water pressure turns minerals into glucose
questions.correctAnswer: The ions may need to move against their concentration gradient using energy
questions.explanation: Active transport uses energy from respiration to move substances from lower concentration to higher concentration.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain active transport in relation to mineral uptake by plants.

questions.prompt: An athlete sweats during a long race. Which homeostatic role does sweating support?
options: Maintaining body temperature through evaporative cooling
Increasing the number of red blood cells instantly
Turning lactic acid into oxygen at the skin
Preventing all water loss from the body
questions.correctAnswer: Maintaining body temperature through evaporative cooling
questions.explanation: Evaporation of sweat removes heat from the skin. This helps keep internal body temperature within a narrow range.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate sweating to thermoregulation in humans.

questions.prompt: Why can a plant cell become turgid in fresh water while an animal cell may burst?
options: The plant cell wall resists bursting as water enters
Animal cells have chloroplasts that pump water inward
Plant cells lack a cell membrane
Fresh water removes all cytoplasm from plant cells
questions.correctAnswer: The plant cell wall resists bursting as water enters
questions.explanation: Both cells can gain water by osmosis, but the rigid plant cell wall provides support and pressure against further swelling.
questions.subStrandTitle: Osmosis in Plant and Animal Cells
questions.learningOutcome: Compare osmotic effects in plant and animal cells.

questions.prompt: How can long-term high blood glucose damage kidney function?
options: It can damage small blood vessels and filtering units in the kidneys
It changes urine into bile before filtration
It stops the heart from pumping blood to the lungs only
It makes the kidneys produce red blood cells instead of urine
questions.correctAnswer: It can damage small blood vessels and filtering units in the kidneys
questions.explanation: Persistently high glucose can harm capillaries and nephrons, reducing the kidneys' ability to filter blood effectively.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how disrupted homeostasis can affect organ function.

questions.prompt: Which model best represents negative feedback control in the body?
options: A thermostat switches a heater off when the room becomes too warm
A door remains open whether the room is hot or cold
A lamp becomes brighter whenever the battery weakens
A thermometer changes the room temperature by itself
questions.correctAnswer: A thermostat switches a heater off when the room becomes too warm
questions.explanation: Negative feedback reverses a change and returns a condition toward a set range, similar to a thermostat controlling heat.
questions.learningOutcome: Use models to represent negative feedback in homeostasis.

questions.prompt: Why are many enzymes sensitive to changes in pH?
options: Extreme pH can change the shape of the active site
pH changes the enzyme into a mineral ion
All enzymes work only in pure water at pH 7
pH removes the need for substrates
questions.correctAnswer: Extreme pH can change the shape of the active site
questions.explanation: Enzyme activity depends on the shape of the active site. Large pH changes can denature the enzyme and reduce activity.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the effect of pH on enzyme activity.

questions.prompt: Where does chemical digestion of starch begin in the human digestive system?
options: Mouth
Stomach
Large intestine
Rectum
questions.correctAnswer: Mouth
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase in the mouth begins breaking starch into smaller sugars during chewing.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify where digestion of major food substances begins.

questions.prompt: Which description best defines a balanced diet?
options: Food containing all required nutrients in suitable proportions
Food made only from carbohydrates
Food eaten once a day regardless of nutrients
Food with no water or minerals
questions.correctAnswer: Food containing all required nutrients in suitable proportions
questions.explanation: A balanced diet supplies energy, body-building nutrients, protective nutrients, water, and fibre in amounts suitable for health.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the components and importance of a balanced diet.

questions.prompt: Why does the small intestine have many villi?
options: To increase surface area for absorption of digested food
To grind food into smaller pieces
To store bile before it reaches the stomach
To produce oxygen for red blood cells
questions.correctAnswer: To increase surface area for absorption of digested food
questions.explanation: Villi provide a large surface area and a good blood supply, making absorption of digested nutrients efficient.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain adaptations of the small intestine for absorption.

questions.prompt: A food sample turns Benedict's solution brick-red after heating. Which nutrient is indicated?
options: Reducing sugar
Protein
Fat
Vitamin C
questions.correctAnswer: Reducing sugar
questions.explanation: Benedict's solution changes from blue to green, yellow, orange, or brick-red when heated with reducing sugars.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret results from common food tests.

questions.prompt: Which word equation summarizes aerobic respiration?
options: Glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy
Carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen
Protein + oxygen -> starch + bile
Water + nitrogen -> glucose + lactic acid
questions.correctAnswer: Glucose + oxygen -> carbon dioxide + water + energy
questions.explanation: Aerobic respiration breaks down glucose using oxygen and releases energy, with carbon dioxide and water as products.
questions.learningOutcome: Represent aerobic respiration using a word equation.

questions.prompt: During vigorous exercise, muscles may produce lactic acid. What condition leads to this?
options: Oxygen supply becomes too low for fully aerobic respiration
The lungs stop all gas exchange permanently
Glucose changes directly into protein in the skin
Sweat glands absorb carbon dioxide from air
questions.correctAnswer: Oxygen supply becomes too low for fully aerobic respiration
questions.explanation: When oxygen delivery cannot meet demand, some muscle cells release energy anaerobically and produce lactic acid.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain lactic acid production during intense exercise.

questions.prompt: Why can boiling drinking water kill cholera-causing bacteria but fail to remove dissolved lead ions?
options: Heat kills many microorganisms but dissolved ions remain in the water
Boiling changes lead ions into harmless oxygen gas
Bacteria and lead ions are both removed by evaporation only
Lead ions are living organisms that reproduce faster when heated
questions.correctAnswer: Heat kills many microorganisms but dissolved ions remain in the water
questions.explanation: Boiling disinfects water by heat, but dissolved chemical contaminants require methods such as suitable filtration or treatment.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse strengths and limits of water treatment methods.

questions.prompt: A food vendor keeps cooked beans warm for several hours before serving. What is the main food safety risk?
options: Bacteria may multiply rapidly in warm food
The beans will immediately become radioactive
Proteins in beans turn into glass
All minerals evaporate from the food
questions.correctAnswer: Bacteria may multiply rapidly in warm food
questions.explanation: Warm, moist cooked food can support fast microbial growth if it is kept for long periods without safe temperature control.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate food storage practices for microbial risk.

questions.prompt: Which plan best reduces malaria cases around a school compound?
options: Drain stagnant water, use bed nets, educate learners, and seek prompt treatment
Spray perfume in classrooms and ignore mosquito breeding sites
Close all windows during the day only
Use antibiotics for every fever without diagnosis
questions.correctAnswer: Drain stagnant water, use bed nets, educate learners, and seek prompt treatment
questions.explanation: Malaria prevention is strongest when vector control, personal protection, health education, and timely care are combined.
questions.learningOutcome: Design integrated strategies for preventing vector-borne disease.

questions.prompt: How can vaccination help protect a community, not only the vaccinated person?
options: It reduces the number of people likely to spread the disease
It makes mosquitoes unable to breed in water
It replaces the need for clean water
It changes bacteria into vitamins
questions.correctAnswer: It reduces the number of people likely to spread the disease
questions.explanation: When many people are immune, disease transmission becomes less likely, helping protect people who may be vulnerable.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how vaccination supports public health.

questions.prompt: What hereditary material is found in chromosomes?
options: DNA
Starch
Cellulose
Bile
questions.correctAnswer: DNA
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are made mainly of DNA and proteins. DNA carries genetic information used in inheritance.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify DNA as the hereditary material in chromosomes.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes a gene?
options: A section of DNA that carries information for a trait or protein
A type of blood vessel found only in plants
A mineral salt stored in bones
A food test reagent used for starch
questions.correctAnswer: A section of DNA that carries information for a trait or protein
questions.explanation: Genes are units of heredity. They contain coded instructions that influence traits through the proteins or products they specify.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the relationship between genes, DNA, and inherited traits.

questions.prompt: Why is meiosis important in sexual reproduction?
options: It produces gametes with half the normal chromosome number
It doubles the chromosome number in body cells every hour
It changes all genes into enzymes
It produces identical cells for wound healing only
questions.correctAnswer: It produces gametes with half the normal chromosome number
questions.explanation: Meiosis forms haploid gametes. Fertilisation then restores the diploid chromosome number in the offspring.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe the role of meiosis in maintaining chromosome number across generations.

questions.prompt: In a monohybrid cross between two heterozygous parents, Tt x Tt, what is the probability of an offspring being tt?
options: 1 in 4
1 in 2
3 in 4
4 in 4
questions.correctAnswer: 1 in 4
questions.explanation: The possible genotypes are TT, Tt, Tt, and tt. One of the four combinations is tt.
questions.learningOutcome: Use a Punnett square to predict genotype probability.

questions.prompt: Which process helps explain why siblings from the same parents are genetically different?
options: Independent assortment of chromosomes during meiosis
Boiling of gametes during fertilisation
Digestion of DNA in the stomach
Evaporation of chromosomes from body cells
questions.correctAnswer: Independent assortment of chromosomes during meiosis
questions.explanation: During meiosis, chromosomes are distributed into gametes in different combinations, creating variation among offspring.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate meiosis to genetic variation in offspring.

questions.prompt: A farmer chooses high-milk-yield cows and healthy bulls for breeding. Which scientific idea is being applied?
options: Selective breeding
Neutralisation
Electrolysis
Transpiration
questions.correctAnswer: Selective breeding
questions.explanation: Selective breeding involves choosing parents with desired traits so those traits are more likely to appear in offspring.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply inheritance concepts to livestock and crop improvement.

questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports the idea that a plant height difference is environmental rather than genetic?
options: Clones of the same plant grow differently when given different fertiliser levels
Plants from different species have different flower colours
A tall plant and a short plant have different chromosome numbers
Seeds from two varieties grow apart in separate counties
questions.correctAnswer: Clones of the same plant grow differently when given different fertiliser levels
questions.explanation: Clones have the same genetic makeup, so differences under different fertiliser levels point strongly to environmental influence.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse evidence for genetic and environmental causes of variation.

questions.prompt: A trait appears in a child although neither parent shows it. What inheritance pattern could explain this?
options: The trait is recessive and both parents are carriers
The trait is caused by a fuse in a circuit
The child has no chromosomes
The trait must be caused only by diet
questions.correctAnswer: The trait is recessive and both parents are carriers
questions.explanation: A recessive trait can be hidden in carriers and appear when a child inherits the recessive allele from both parents.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse simple family inheritance patterns involving recessive traits.

questions.prompt: Which biotechnology strategy can ethically support food security for banana farmers?
options: Use tissue culture to produce disease-free planting materials and train farmers on safe handling
Release untested organisms into farms without monitoring
Ban all crop records and ignore disease symptoms
Select planting material only by fruit colour in the market
questions.correctAnswer: Use tissue culture to produce disease-free planting materials and train farmers on safe handling
questions.explanation: Tissue culture can multiply clean planting materials, but responsible use also needs training, monitoring, and attention to local farming needs.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate biotechnology applications for agriculture and food security.

questions.prompt: Why can a mutation be harmful, neutral, or beneficial?
options: Its effect depends on the gene changed and the environment
Every mutation immediately kills the organism
Mutations only happen in non-living objects
A mutation always produces the same visible trait
questions.correctAnswer: Its effect depends on the gene changed and the environment
questions.explanation: A mutation changes genetic information. Its impact depends on whether it affects function and whether the environment favours the change.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain possible effects of mutation on organisms.

questions.prompt: What does the atomic number of an element represent?
options: Number of protons in each atom
Number of molecules in a sample
Mass of one litre of the element
Number of compounds it can form
questions.correctAnswer: Number of protons in each atom
questions.explanation: The atomic number is the proton number. It identifies the element and determines its place in the periodic table.
questions.learningOutcome: State the meaning of atomic number.

questions.prompt: Which statement describes isotopes of the same element?
options: They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
They have different numbers of protons and the same mass number
They are compounds with identical formulas
They are atoms with no nucleus
questions.correctAnswer: They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
questions.explanation: Isotopes are atoms of the same element, so they have the same proton number, but their neutron numbers differ.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe isotopes using protons and neutrons.

questions.prompt: Why do Group 1 metals commonly form ions with a +1 charge?
options: They lose one outer electron
They gain seven protons
They share all electrons equally with water
They have no electrons in neutral atoms
questions.correctAnswer: They lose one outer electron
questions.explanation: Group 1 atoms have one valence electron. Losing it gives a stable positive ion with a single positive charge.
questions.learningOutcome: Relate group number to ion formation in metals.

questions.prompt: What is the relative molecular mass of carbon dioxide, CO2, if C = 12 and O = 16?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide has one carbon atom and two oxygen atoms, so its relative molecular mass is 12 + 16 + 16 = 44.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate relative molecular mass from atomic masses.

questions.prompt: What type of bonding is formed in sodium chloride?
options: Ionic bonding through electron transfer
Covalent bonding through equal sharing only
Metallic bonding between two non-metals
Hydrogen bonding inside sodium atoms
questions.correctAnswer: Ionic bonding through electron transfer
questions.explanation: Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine, forming oppositely charged ions that attract each other in an ionic lattice.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe ionic bonding in simple compounds.

questions.prompt: Why do metals conduct electricity when solid?
options: They contain delocalised electrons that can move through the structure
Their atoms have no nuclei
They dissolve in air to form ions
Their protons move freely from atom to atom
questions.correctAnswer: They contain delocalised electrons that can move through the structure
questions.explanation: Metallic bonding includes mobile delocalised electrons. These electrons carry charge through the solid metal.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain electrical conductivity in metals using bonding structure.

questions.prompt: Why does graphite conduct electricity while diamond does not, although both are forms of carbon?
options: Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers, while diamond's electrons are fixed in covalent bonds
Diamond contains sodium ions, while graphite contains no atoms
Graphite is always liquid at room temperature
Diamond has no covalent bonds
questions.correctAnswer: Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers, while diamond's electrons are fixed in covalent bonds
questions.explanation: In graphite, one electron from each carbon atom can move along layers. In diamond, electrons are held in a rigid covalent network.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how bonding and structure affect properties of carbon allotropes.

questions.prompt: Neon is very unreactive under normal conditions. Which explanation best accounts for this?
options: Its outer electron shell is full
It has no protons in the nucleus
It is always bonded to sodium
It dissolves all metals instantly
questions.correctAnswer: Its outer electron shell is full
questions.explanation: Noble gases such as neon have stable outer electron arrangements, so they have little tendency to gain, lose, or share electrons.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse chemical stability using electron arrangement.

questions.prompt: Which explanation best accounts for water having a much higher boiling point than methane?
options: Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other
Methane contains more oxygen atoms than water
Water has no intermolecular forces
Methane molecules are giant ionic lattices
questions.correctAnswer: Water molecules form hydrogen bonds with each other
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules are relatively strong intermolecular forces, so more energy is needed for boiling.
questions.learningOutcome: Use intermolecular forces to explain differences in boiling point.

questions.prompt: How can a mixture of sand, salt, and water be separated most suitably in a school laboratory?
options: Filter to remove sand, then evaporate water to obtain salt
Use a magnet to attract salt, then burn sand
Add acid to change sand into salt
Freeze the mixture and throw away the ice
questions.correctAnswer: Filter to remove sand, then evaporate water to obtain salt
questions.explanation: Sand is insoluble and can be filtered out. Dissolved salt can be recovered from the filtrate by evaporating the water.
questions.learningOutcome: Select appropriate methods for separating common mixtures.

questions.prompt: What does a pH value below 7 usually indicate?
options: An acidic solution
A neutral solution
An alkaline solution
A pure metal
questions.correctAnswer: An acidic solution
questions.explanation: On the pH scale, values below 7 are acidic, 7 is neutral, and values above 7 are alkaline.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret pH values for acidic, neutral, and alkaline solutions.

questions.prompt: What are the usual products when an acid reacts completely with a base?
options: Salt and water
Oxygen and hydrogen
Glucose and starch
Carbon and nitrogen
questions.correctAnswer: Salt and water
questions.explanation: Neutralisation between an acid and a base forms water and a salt whose ions come from the reacting acid and base.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe products of acid-base neutralisation reactions.

questions.prompt: What is the role of a catalyst in a chemical reaction?
options: It increases reaction rate without being used up overall
It changes every product into water
It stops particles from colliding
It makes a reaction ignore temperature
questions.correctAnswer: It increases reaction rate without being used up overall
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative pathway with lower activation energy and is regenerated during the reaction.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how catalysts affect reaction rates.

questions.prompt: Which equation is balanced for magnesium reacting with oxygen to form magnesium oxide?
options: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO
Mg + O2 -> MgO
Mg2 + O -> MgO2
2MgO -> Mg + O2
questions.correctAnswer: 2Mg + O2 -> 2MgO
questions.explanation: The balanced equation has two magnesium atoms and two oxygen atoms on both sides.
questions.learningOutcome: Balance simple chemical equations by conserving atoms.

questions.prompt: How many moles are present in 5.6 g of iron if the relative atomic mass of iron is 56?
options: 0.10 mol
10 mol
56 mol
questions.correctAnswer: 0.10 mol
questions.explanation: Amount in moles equals mass divided by molar mass. 5.6 divided by 56 gives 0.10 mol.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate amount of substance from mass and relative atomic mass.

questions.prompt: In an acid-base titration, why is an indicator added to the flask?
options: To show when the reaction is near the end point
To make the burette read zero automatically
To remove all salt from the solution
To increase the volume of acid secretly
questions.correctAnswer: To show when the reaction is near the end point
questions.explanation: An indicator changes colour over a particular pH range, helping show when neutralisation is nearly complete.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the use of indicators in acid-base titration.

questions.prompt: Why do crushed marble chips react faster with dilute hydrochloric acid than large marble chips of the same mass?
options: Crushed chips have a larger surface area exposed to acid
Crushed chips have fewer calcium carbonate particles
Large chips contain no carbonate ions
Surface area has no effect on collision frequency
questions.correctAnswer: Crushed chips have a larger surface area exposed to acid
questions.explanation: Increasing surface area allows more acid particles to collide with marble particles each second, increasing reaction rate.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how surface area affects reaction rate.

questions.prompt: For the equilibrium N2 + 3H2 <-> 2NH3, why does increasing pressure favour ammonia formation?
options: The product side has fewer gas molecules
The reactant side has no gas molecules
Pressure changes nitrogen into a liquid metal
Ammonia formation produces more gas molecules
questions.correctAnswer: The product side has fewer gas molecules
questions.explanation: Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas particles. Two ammonia molecules are fewer than four reactant molecules.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse the effect of pressure on gaseous equilibrium systems.

questions.prompt: Which plan best compares the effectiveness of two antacid tablets?
options: Add equal masses to equal volumes of the same acid and compare final pH or acid neutralised
Use different acids, different tablet masses, and no measurements
Taste both tablets and choose the sweeter one
Compare only the colours of the tablet packets
questions.correctAnswer: Add equal masses to equal volumes of the same acid and compare final pH or acid neutralised
questions.explanation: A fair comparison controls tablet mass and acid conditions while measuring a change linked to neutralisation.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a controlled investigation for comparing neutralising capacity.

questions.prompt: Why should acid be added slowly to water, rather than water poured into concentrated acid?
options: Dilution releases heat and slow addition to water reduces splashing risk
Water makes acids colder by removing all ions
Acid cannot mix with water under any conditions
Adding acid to water creates explosive oxygen only
questions.correctAnswer: Dilution releases heat and slow addition to water reduces splashing risk
questions.explanation: Diluting concentrated acid is exothermic. Adding acid slowly to a larger volume of water helps disperse heat safely.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain safe procedures for diluting acids.

questions.prompt: Which formula gives average speed?
options: Distance divided by time
Mass divided by volume
Force multiplied by area
Current divided by voltage
questions.correctAnswer: Distance divided by time
questions.explanation: Average speed is calculated by dividing total distance travelled by total time taken.
questions.learningOutcome: State the relationship between speed, distance, and time.

questions.prompt: What does acceleration measure?
options: Rate of change of velocity
Total distance only
Amount of matter in an object
Pressure in a liquid only
questions.correctAnswer: Rate of change of velocity
questions.explanation: Acceleration describes how quickly velocity changes with time, including changes in speed or direction.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain acceleration as change in velocity per unit time.

questions.prompt: Which statement expresses Newton's third law of motion?
options: For every action force, there is an equal and opposite reaction force on another body
An object at rest has no mass
Energy is destroyed whenever friction acts
Acceleration is always zero when speed is high
questions.correctAnswer: For every action force, there is an equal and opposite reaction force on another body
questions.explanation: Newton's third law describes force pairs that act on different bodies and are equal in size but opposite in direction.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe Newton's third law using interacting bodies.

questions.prompt: A cyclist travels 150 m in 10 s. What is the cyclist's average speed?
options: 15 m/s
questions.correctAnswer: 15 m/s
questions.explanation: Average speed equals distance divided by time. 150 m divided by 10 s gives 15 m/s.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate average speed from distance and time data.

questions.prompt: A force of 20 N moves a trolley 3 m in the direction of the force. How much work is done?
questions.explanation: Work done equals force multiplied by distance moved in the force direction. 20 N multiplied by 3 m gives 60 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate work done from force and distance.

questions.prompt: A 500 W motor runs for 40 s. How much energy does it transfer?
questions.explanation: Energy transferred equals power multiplied by time. 500 W multiplied by 40 s equals 20000 J.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate energy transferred from power and time.

questions.prompt: Why do seat belts reduce injury during a sudden stop?
options: They increase stopping time and reduce the average force on the body
They remove the passenger's mass
They make the car have no momentum
They change kinetic energy into extra fuel
questions.correctAnswer: They increase stopping time and reduce the average force on the body
questions.explanation: For a given change in momentum, increasing the time of impact reduces the average force experienced.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse safety devices using force, time, and momentum ideas.

questions.prompt: What does a straight line with positive gradient on a velocity-time graph show?
options: Constant acceleration
Constant displacement
Zero velocity throughout
Changing mass
questions.correctAnswer: Constant acceleration
questions.explanation: The gradient of a velocity-time graph represents acceleration. A straight positive gradient shows constant acceleration.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret velocity-time graphs for acceleration.

questions.prompt: Which bicycle design choice best improves braking safety on wet roads?
options: Tyres with good tread and brakes adjusted to increase friction without locking the wheels
Smooth tyres coated with oil
Removing one brake to reduce mass
Using plastic rims that soften in sunlight
questions.correctAnswer: Tyres with good tread and brakes adjusted to increase friction without locking the wheels
questions.explanation: Good tread improves grip, and controlled braking helps avoid skidding while still increasing friction enough to slow the bicycle.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply friction concepts to design safer transport solutions.

questions.prompt: Why do simple machines such as levers not create energy?
options: They trade force and distance, with some energy lost through friction
They multiply input energy without limit
They remove gravity from the load
They convert all matter into energy
questions.correctAnswer: They trade force and distance, with some energy lost through friction
questions.explanation: Machines can make work easier by changing force or distance, but they cannot output more energy than is put in.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain energy transfer and efficiency in simple machines.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of electric current?
options: Ampere
Volt
Ohm
Coulomb
questions.correctAnswer: Ampere
questions.explanation: Electric current is measured in amperes. It describes the rate at which electric charge flows.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify the SI unit of electric current.

questions.prompt: Which relationship is stated by Ohm's law for a conductor at constant temperature?
options: V = IR
P = mgh
F = ma
Density = mass/volume
questions.correctAnswer: V = IR
questions.explanation: Ohm's law states that potential difference equals current multiplied by resistance for an ohmic conductor at constant temperature.
questions.learningOutcome: State Ohm's law and identify its quantities.

questions.prompt: How does a fuse protect an electrical circuit?
options: It melts and breaks the circuit when current is too high
It stores unlimited charge for later use
It changes alternating current into sound
It removes the need for insulation
questions.correctAnswer: It melts and breaks the circuit when current is too high
questions.explanation: A fuse contains a thin wire that heats and melts if excessive current flows, disconnecting the circuit.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain the protective function of a fuse.

questions.prompt: A resistor has a potential difference of 12 V across it and a current of 3 A through it. What is its resistance?
options: 4 ohms
36 ohms
15 ohms
0.25 ohms
questions.correctAnswer: 4 ohms
questions.explanation: Using R = V/I, resistance is 12 V divided by 3 A, which gives 4 ohms.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate resistance from potential difference and current.

questions.prompt: Two 6 ohm resistors are connected in parallel. What is their combined resistance?
options: 3 ohms
12 ohms
6 ohms
36 ohms
questions.correctAnswer: 3 ohms
questions.explanation: For two equal resistors in parallel, the combined resistance is half of one resistor. Half of 6 ohms is 3 ohms.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate total resistance for simple parallel circuits.

questions.prompt: What happens in an ideal step-up transformer?
options: Output voltage increases while output current decreases
Both voltage and current increase without energy input
Direct current is produced from a dry cell
The core changes into copper wire
questions.correctAnswer: Output voltage increases while output current decreases
questions.explanation: A step-up transformer has more turns on the secondary coil, increasing voltage. In an ideal transformer, power is conserved, so current decreases.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe voltage and current changes in a step-up transformer.

questions.prompt: Why is electrical power transmitted over long distances at high voltage?
options: High voltage allows lower current, reducing heating losses in cables
High voltage makes resistance zero in every cable
High voltage changes copper into an insulator
High voltage prevents all storms from affecting lines
questions.correctAnswer: High voltage allows lower current, reducing heating losses in cables
questions.explanation: For the same power, increasing voltage lowers current. Lower current reduces energy lost as heat in transmission wires.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse why high voltage is used in power transmission.

questions.prompt: Why are classroom lights usually wired in parallel rather than in series?
options: Each light can receive the supply voltage and operate independently
Parallel circuits make bulbs require no energy
Series circuits always prevent current flow
Parallel wiring removes the need for switches
questions.correctAnswer: Each light can receive the supply voltage and operate independently
questions.explanation: In parallel, each lamp has its own path across the supply. One lamp can fail or be switched off without turning off all others.
questions.learningOutcome: Compare series and parallel arrangements for practical wiring.

questions.prompt: Which method best estimates the focal length of a convex lens using sunlight safely?
options: Focus light from a distant object onto a screen and measure the lens-to-screen distance
Look directly at the Sun through the lens
Put the lens in water and measure its mass
Rub the lens on cloth until it becomes magnetic
questions.correctAnswer: Focus light from a distant object onto a screen and measure the lens-to-screen distance
questions.explanation: A distant object forms an image near the focal plane. The safe method uses a screen and avoids looking at the Sun through the lens.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a safe method for estimating focal length of a convex lens.

questions.prompt: Why can sound not travel through a vacuum?
options: Sound needs particles of a medium to transmit vibrations
Sound is made only of visible light
Vacuum has too much air pressure
Sound waves are stationary objects
questions.correctAnswer: Sound needs particles of a medium to transmit vibrations
questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave. It travels by vibrating particles in a medium such as air, water, or solids.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain why sound requires a material medium.

questions.prompt: Which gas is a greenhouse gas?
options: Carbon dioxide
Argon
Neon
Helium
questions.correctAnswer: Carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide absorbs infrared radiation and contributes to the greenhouse effect in the atmosphere.
questions.learningOutcome: Identify examples of greenhouse gases.

questions.prompt: In the water cycle, what is the process called when water vapour changes into liquid droplets?
options: Condensation
Transpiration
Infiltration
Sublimation
questions.correctAnswer: Condensation
questions.explanation: Condensation occurs when water vapour cools and changes into liquid droplets, helping form clouds.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe key processes in the water cycle.

questions.prompt: How do excess nitrates and phosphates from farms contribute to eutrophication in a lake?
options: They promote algal blooms that can reduce oxygen in the water
They turn all fish into algae immediately
They remove all water from the lake
They make the lake water boil at room temperature
questions.correctAnswer: They promote algal blooms that can reduce oxygen in the water
questions.explanation: Excess nutrients encourage rapid algal growth. Decomposition of algae can use up oxygen and harm aquatic life.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how nutrient pollution affects aquatic ecosystems.

questions.prompt: A soil sample has pH 4.8 and is too acidic for beans. Which amendment would most directly reduce the acidity?
options: Agricultural lime
More acidic fertiliser
Table sugar
Plastic mulch only
questions.correctAnswer: Agricultural lime
questions.explanation: Agricultural lime is alkaline and can neutralise excess soil acidity, raising pH toward a suitable range for many crops.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply pH knowledge to soil management decisions.

questions.prompt: A quadrat survey finds 240 grass plants in an area of 60 m2. What is the population density?
options: 4 plants per m2
300 plants per m2
0.25 plants per m2
180 plants per m2
questions.correctAnswer: 4 plants per m2
questions.explanation: Population density equals number of organisms divided by area. 240 divided by 60 gives 4 plants per m2.
questions.learningOutcome: Calculate population density from quadrat data.

questions.prompt: What happens in a biogas digester?
options: Microorganisms break down organic waste without oxygen to produce methane-rich gas
Sunlight changes plastic directly into petrol
Water splits into hydrogen and oxygen without energy
Sand turns into limestone by cooling
questions.correctAnswer: Microorganisms break down organic waste without oxygen to produce methane-rich gas
questions.explanation: Biogas is produced by anaerobic decomposition of organic matter such as manure and food waste.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain how organic waste can be converted into biogas.

questions.prompt: How do mangrove forests help protect coastal environments?
options: Their roots reduce wave energy, trap sediments, and provide habitats
They increase plastic pollution in seawater
They remove all salt from the ocean
They stop tides from occurring
questions.correctAnswer: Their roots reduce wave energy, trap sediments, and provide habitats
questions.explanation: Mangrove roots stabilise shorelines, slow water movement, trap sediments, and support many species.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse ecosystem services provided by mangrove forests.

questions.prompt: A remote school is choosing between a solar water pump and a diesel pump. Which comparison is most scientific?
options: Compare water output, initial cost, running cost, emissions, maintenance, and energy availability
Choose the pump with the brightest paint
Use diesel because all pumps must burn fuel
Use solar because it works at full power every night without storage
questions.correctAnswer: Compare water output, initial cost, running cost, emissions, maintenance, and energy availability
questions.explanation: A good technology decision uses evidence about performance, cost, reliability, and environmental impact.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse scientific and sustainability factors in energy technology choices.

questions.prompt: Which school laboratory plan best reduces chemical waste?
options: Use microscale experiments, label waste containers, neutralise where appropriate, and follow disposal guidelines
Pour all chemicals into the sink at the end of every lesson
Mix unknown chemicals to reduce the number of bottles
Burn all liquid waste in an open classroom
questions.correctAnswer: Use microscale experiments, label waste containers, neutralise where appropriate, and follow disposal guidelines
questions.explanation: Waste reduction combines smaller quantities, separation of waste types, suitable treatment, and safe disposal procedures.
questions.learningOutcome: Design safe and sustainable approaches to laboratory waste management.

questions.prompt: Why can climate change affect the distribution of malaria?
options: Temperature and rainfall changes can alter mosquito breeding and survival conditions
Malaria parasites feed only on carbon dioxide in clouds
Warmer weather makes all diseases disappear
Climate affects rocks but never living organisms
questions.correctAnswer: Temperature and rainfall changes can alter mosquito breeding and survival conditions
questions.explanation: Mosquitoes and parasites are influenced by temperature, rainfall, and water availability, so changing climate can shift disease risk zones.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain links between climate factors and vector-borne disease risk.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of pasteurising milk?
options: To reduce harmful microorganisms while keeping the milk usable
To change milk into a metal
To remove all water and make salt
To make milk radioactive for storage
questions.correctAnswer: To reduce harmful microorganisms while keeping the milk usable
questions.explanation: Pasteurisation uses controlled heating to reduce disease-causing microorganisms without severely damaging the quality of milk.
questions.learningOutcome: State the purpose of pasteurisation in food safety.

questions.prompt: What is biofortification in crop science?
options: Increasing nutrient content of crops through breeding or biotechnology
Adding plastic beads to soil to make crops shiny
Removing all minerals from grain
Growing crops without sunlight or water
questions.correctAnswer: Increasing nutrient content of crops through breeding or biotechnology
questions.explanation: Biofortification aims to improve the nutritional value of staple crops, such as increasing vitamin or mineral content.
questions.learningOutcome: Explain biofortification as a science-based approach to nutrition.

questions.prompt: How can remote sensing support crop management?
options: It can use reflected light data to monitor crop health and stress
It replaces seeds with computer files
It makes crops grow without soil nutrients
It prevents clouds from forming over farms
questions.correctAnswer: It can use reflected light data to monitor crop health and stress
questions.explanation: Sensors on satellites, drones, or aircraft can detect patterns linked to plant health, moisture, and stress.
questions.learningOutcome: Describe how sensor data can inform agricultural decisions.

questions.prompt: A disinfectant label recommends 10 mL of concentrate per litre of water. How much concentrate is needed for 5 litres of water?
options: 50 mL
5 mL
10 mL
500 mL
questions.correctAnswer: 50 mL
questions.explanation: The amount scales with volume. 10 mL per litre multiplied by 5 litres gives 50 mL.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply ratio reasoning to prepare safe working solutions.

questions.prompt: A water test shows high turbidity. What does this most likely mean?
options: The water contains many suspended particles
The water has no particles at all
The water is pure ethanol
The water has zero temperature
questions.correctAnswer: The water contains many suspended particles
questions.explanation: Turbidity measures cloudiness caused by suspended matter such as soil, organic particles, or microorganisms.
questions.learningOutcome: Interpret water quality indicators used in community health.

questions.prompt: Why does a dark surface improve the performance of a simple solar dryer?
options: It absorbs more radiant energy and converts more of it into heat
It reflects all sunlight away from the dryer
It produces electricity without any device
It prevents evaporation of water from food
questions.correctAnswer: It absorbs more radiant energy and converts more of it into heat
questions.explanation: Dark surfaces absorb a larger fraction of incoming radiation, raising temperature and helping moisture evaporate from food.
questions.learningOutcome: Apply energy absorption concepts to solar food preservation.

questions.prompt: Why can uncontrolled use of antibiotics increase resistant bacteria in a population?
options: Susceptible bacteria die while resistant bacteria survive and reproduce
Antibiotics turn all bacteria into viruses
Resistance disappears whenever medicine is misused
Antibiotics make bacteria unable to pass traits to offspring
questions.correctAnswer: Susceptible bacteria die while resistant bacteria survive and reproduce
questions.explanation: Antibiotic misuse creates selection pressure. Resistant bacteria are more likely to survive and pass on resistance traits.
questions.learningOutcome: Analyse how selection pressure contributes to antimicrobial resistance.

questions.prompt: Why is open burning of plastic waste a poor waste-management practice?
options: It can release harmful fumes and wastes useful material that could be reduced, reused, or recycled
It turns all plastics into clean drinking water
It removes the need for waste sorting forever
It produces only oxygen and nitrogen
questions.correctAnswer: It can release harmful fumes and wastes useful material that could be reduced, reused, or recycled
questions.explanation: Open burning can expose people to toxic smoke and loses resources that may be managed through safer circular approaches.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate environmental and health impacts of waste-management choices.

questions.prompt: Which low-cost system would best improve safety of turbid water for a school camping activity?
options: Allow settling, filter through clean layers, disinfect by boiling or chlorination, and store in a clean covered container
Add soil to hide the particles and drink immediately
Use only colour to judge safety
Cool the water in shade and skip treatment
questions.correctAnswer: Allow settling, filter through clean layers, disinfect by boiling or chlorination, and store in a clean covered container
questions.explanation: A combined system removes many suspended particles, kills many pathogens, and reduces recontamination during storage.
questions.learningOutcome: Design a simple multi-barrier approach for safer water use.

questions.prompt: Why should scientific claims in adverts be checked against evidence?
options: Evidence from fair tests helps prevent misleading conclusions
Adverts always contain complete laboratory reports
Science does not use measurements
A claim becomes true when many people repeat it
questions.correctAnswer: Evidence from fair tests helps prevent misleading conclusions
questions.explanation: Scientific claims should be supported by reliable data from fair methods, not only by popularity or persuasive language.
questions.learningOutcome: Evaluate everyday scientific claims using evidence and fair testing.
